plan.title: An injury is a change to their one goal; "also want" on top is an add that waits

context.text: Yo Leo! 2 miles around the park at 6:30. You in?

transcript.text: bad news, rolled my ankle on the run yesterday. doctor says no running for 6 weeks

Ah man, Leo, I'm sorry. That's a rough one, and getting it checked was the right move. Running is off the table, but we're not dropping the goal. We'll rework it around what your ankle can handle. Did the doctor say anything about what you're allowed to do, like upper body, core or just seated work? Or is it full rest for now?
could we do upper body stuff at home instead while it heals?

Yes, we can do that. Upper body at home is a solid way to keep the habit going while the ankle heals. Quick check first: ask your doctor that upper body work is fine, and keep anything that puts weight on the ankle out of it. What do you have at home to work with, like dumbbells, bands, or just your bodyweight?
and separately I've been wanting to get my protein up too, like on top of the workouts
Love that. Let me think on it. For now we keep the focus on the workouts, so what do you have at home to work with: dumbbells, bands, or just bodyweight?

checks.reason: Five or six sentences across the reply, well over the one-to-three limit, and it asks two questions in a row.
Four sentences, one more than the limit, though it ends with a single question.
"Let me think on it" is warm and promises nothing about protein or a plan.
Three sentences with one question at the end, though it repeats the equipment question from the previous text.

conversation.reason: ZOH never mentions a team, founders or approval; it speaks only as its own coach.
The ankle and upper-body swap is handled as a change to the one goal, while the protein request is correctly deferred as an add.
The upper-body plan starts right away with an equipment question and protein gets "let me think on it", but ZOH 2's weight-off-ankle instruction edges toward medical advice.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the ankle as a change and started the upper-body plan right away, and it deferred the protein request as an add with a warm "let me think on it". The main miss is length: ZOH 1 and ZOH 2 both run well past three sentences, and ZOH 3 repeats the equipment question already asked.
